title: Reducedness and local Noetherianity from an fppf scheme cover
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Stacks in groupoids, their morphisms and 2-fibre products use [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]; algebraic spaces use [def-trf-algebraic-space]. An algebraic stack is an fppf stack in groupoids with diagonal representable by algebraic spaces and a smooth surjective scheme atlas [def-pc-fppf-site, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. A morphism is representable by algebraic spaces if every scheme base change is an algebraic space. For representable maps, flatness, local finite presentation and local finite type are tested after scheme base change on etale scheme charts [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Surjectivity means that every field-valued target object lifts, up to isomorphism, after some field extension [def-weil-field]. Let $\mathcal Z$ be an algebraic stack over $S$ and let $p:V\to\mathcal Z$ be a representable surjective flat locally finitely presented morphism from a scheme $V$. If $V$ is reduced and locally Noetherian, then $\mathcal Z$ admits a smooth surjective scheme atlas which is reduced and locally Noetherian. Reduced for a scheme means that its local rings have no nonzero nilpotent elements; locally Noetherian means that it has an affine open cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [pqf-def-locnoeth]. No smoothness of $p$ and no Noetherian condition on $S$ are assumed.

proof.text: Choose a smooth surjective scheme atlas $q:W\to\mathcal Z$, which exists by the hypothesis that $\mathcal Z$ is algebraic. By representability of $p$, $P=W\times_{\mathcal Z}V$ is an algebraic space. Choose a representable surjective etale scheme chart $e:T\to P$ by [def-trf-algebraic-space]. The projection $P\to V$ is the base change of $q$, and $P\to W$ is the base change of $p$. Apply [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]: the first projection is smooth, the second is flat, locally of finite presentation and surjective, while $e$ is smooth, flat and locally of finite presentation. Composition therefore makes $a:T\to V$ smooth and $b:T\to W$ flat, locally of finite presentation and surjective. Here all maps whose properties are used are representable by algebraic spaces; the two final maps are maps of schemes.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-smooth-reduced-dense-pullback] to the smooth scheme morphism $a:T\to V$. Its base $V$ is reduced and locally Noetherian by hypothesis, so $T$ is reduced and locally Noetherian. This assertion does not require $a$ to be surjective; none of the density conclusions of that node is used.

source.place: Tag 034E (lemma-reduced-local-smooth); Tag 034C (lemma-Noetherian-local-fppf), ascent along a smooth morphism.

proof.text: For every $w\in W$, choose $t\in T$ with $b(t)=w$ using surjectivity of $b$. By [def-weil-flat-morphism], $\mathcal O_{W,w}\to\mathcal O_{T,t}$ is a flat local ring homomorphism. It is faithfully flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-hom-faithfully-flat], hence injective by [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ideal-contraction] with the zero ideal. If $x^n=0$ in $\mathcal O_{W,w}$, for $n\geq1$, its image is nilpotent in the reduced ring $\mathcal O_{T,t}$, so its image is zero and injectivity gives $x=0$. Every local ring of $W$ is thus reduced, which is reducedness of $W$ by [def-pc-reduced-scheme].

Apply [lem-sfb-scheme-locnoeth-fppf-descent] to $b:T\to W$: step 1 supplies flatness, local finite presentation and surjectivity, and step 2 supplies local Noetherianity of $T$. It follows that $W$ is locally Noetherian. Together with step 3, the already chosen smooth surjective atlas $W\to\mathcal Z$ has both required properties. No smoothness of $p$ or Noetherianity of $S$ was used.
